header.title: U.S. energy drink demand set for structural multi-year growth from new occasions

s01_bottom_line.text: U.S. caffeinated beverage spending has grown 6% annually since 2019 (energy drinks 8%, beverage shops 7%), nearly double the broader food and restaurant industry, with net purchase intent for energy drinks at 19% versus about 5% in 2019/2021.
Morgan Stanley Research expects the 6% caffeinated beverage spending pace to continue through 2030, driven by six structural factors supporting energy drink demand.

The article frames energy drinks and beverage shops as structurally advantaged consumer growth categories driven by demographics, innovation and new occasions rather than substitution, but does not quantify the earnings or revenue impact for any specific listed company.

items.text: U.S. spending on caffeinated beverages has grown at a 6% annual rate since 2019.
Energy drinks grew at 8% annually, leading the category.

33% expect to visit a beverage shop more often vs 16% less often, a net positive intent of 17%.
Caffeinated beverage spending growth is nearly double the pace of the broader food and restaurant industry. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

header.title: U.S. energy drink demand set for structural multi-year growth from new occasions

s01_bottom_line.text: U.S. caffeinated beverage spending has grown 6% annually since 2019 (energy drinks 8%, beverage shops 7%), nearly double the broader food and restaurant industry, with net purchase intent for energy drinks at 19% versus about 5% in 2019/2021.
Morgan Stanley Research expects the 6% caffeinated beverage spending pace to continue through 2030, driven by six structural factors supporting energy drink demand.

The article frames energy drinks and beverage shops as structurally advantaged consumer growth categories driven by demographics, innovation and new occasions rather than substitution, but does not quantify the earnings or revenue impact for any specific listed company.

items.text: U.S. spending on caffeinated beverages has grown at a 6% annual rate since 2019.
Energy drinks grew at 8% annually, leading the category.
A net 19% of respondents expect to drink more energy drinks over the next three months, up from about 5% in 2019 and 2021 surveys.
33% expect to visit a beverage shop more often vs 16% less often, a net positive intent of 17%.
Caffeinated beverage spending growth is nearly double the pace of the broader food and restaurant industry. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Beverage shops grew at 7% annually, leading the category.
